collection.label: Manetho, History of Egypt
collection.author_name: Manetho of Sebennytus (c. 280 BCE), quoted by Josephus and Syncellus
collection.search_terms: manetho aegyptiaca history of egypt hyksos shepherd kings avaris dynasties pharaohs josephus syncellus
collection.description: Manetho's history of Egypt, written in Greek about 280 BCE, survives only in quotations. This shelf shows them on the manuscript pages that carry them.

texts.title: Manetho on the Reigns of the Gods and Demigods (George Syncellus)
texts.date_approx: c. 280 BCE (Manetho); Syncellus c. 810 AD; manuscript 11th c.
texts.source: Paris gr. 1711 (11th c.), pp. 11-12, via Gallica IIIF + Müller FHG II Greek (DFHG, checked against the print) + Waddell English (Loeb 1940, public domain)
texts.description: Manetho's list of the gods who ruled Egypt before men, from Hephaestus (Ptah) for 9000 years to Typhon, and of the demigods Horus to Zeus, as quoted by George Syncellus, on the page of Paris gr. 1711 that carries it.

texts.title: Manetho's Dynasties I-XI (Book I), in Africanus and Eusebius (George Syncellus)
texts.date_approx: c. 280 BCE (Manetho); epitomes 3rd-4th c. AD; Syncellus c. 810 AD; manuscript 11th c.
texts.source: Paris gr. 1764 (11th c.), fols. 2r-4v, via Gallica IIIF + Müller FHG II Greek (DFHG, checked against the print) + Waddell English (Loeb 1940, public domain)
texts.description: The first book of Manetho's king list, from Menes to the Eleventh Dynasty, in the two versions of Julius Africanus and Eusebius as copied by George Syncellus, shown on the manuscript pages of Paris gr. 1764.

texts.title: Manetho's Dynasties XII-XIX (Book II): Sesostris, the Shepherd Kings, the Exodus and the Fall of Troy, in Africanus and Eusebius (George Syncellus)
texts.date_approx: c. 280 BCE (Manetho); epitomes 3rd-4th c. AD; Syncellus c. 810 AD; manuscript 11th c.
texts.source: Paris gr. 1764 (11th c.), fols. 4v-5v and 9r-10v, via Gallica IIIF + Müller FHG II Greek (DFHG, checked against the print) + Waddell English (Loeb 1940, public domain)
texts.description: The start of Manetho's second book: the Twelfth Dynasty with Sesostris, conqueror of Asia, and the builder of the Labyrinth, the Thirteenth to Seventeenth Dynasties with the Shepherd Kings (Hyksos), the Eighteenth Dynasty with Amosis and the Exodus, and the Nineteenth Dynasty, ending with Thuoris, in whose reign Troy was taken, in the versions of Africanus and Eusebius, on the manuscript pages of Paris gr. 1764.

texts.title: Manetho on the Hyksos (Josephus, Against Apion 1.73-105)
texts.date_approx: c. 280 BCE (Manetho); quoted by Josephus c. 95 AD; manuscript 10th c.
texts.source: Laur. Plut. 69.22 (10th c.), fols. 6v-8v, via BML Teca Digitale IIIF + Niese Greek (Perseus) + Whiston English (Perseus)
texts.description: Manetho's account of the Hyksos, the 'shepherd kings' who seized Egypt, and of the kings after their expulsion, quoted word for word by Josephus in Against Apion 1.73-105 and shown on the five pages of the oldest manuscript.

texts.title: Manetho on Osarseph and the Lepers (Josephus, Against Apion 1.227-251)
texts.date_approx: c. 280 BCE (Manetho); quoted by Josephus c. 95 AD; manuscript 10th c.
texts.source: Laur. Plut. 69.22 (10th c.), fols. 16r-18r, via BML Teca Digitale IIIF + Niese Greek (Perseus) + Whiston English (Perseus, checked against the 1860 printing)
texts.description: Manetho's story of King Amenophis, the lepers sent to the quarries, the priest Osarseph who led them in revolt from Avaris and was later called Moses, and the thirteen years of their rule, as quoted by Josephus in Against Apion 1.227-251.

texts.title: Manetho's Dynasties XX-XXXI (Book III), in Africanus and Eusebius (George Syncellus)
texts.date_approx: c. 280 BCE (Manetho); epitomes 3rd-4th c. AD; Syncellus c. 810 AD; manuscript 11th c.
texts.source: Paris gr. 1764 (11th c.), fols. 10v-11v, via Gallica IIIF + Müller FHG II Greek (DFHG, checked against the print) + Waddell English (Loeb 1940, public domain)
texts.description: The third book of Manetho's king list, from the Twentieth Dynasty to the Persian kings conquered by Alexander, in the versions of Africanus and Eusebius as copied by George Syncellus, on the manuscript pages of Paris gr. 1764.

authors.name: Manetho of Sebennytus
authors.bio: Egyptian priest of Sebennytus who wrote a history of Egypt in Greek (Aegyptiaca) under the first Ptolemies; his division of Egypt's kings into thirty dynasties is still used.
